title: The Korean Melon Soju Trend: Real Talk from a Seoul Salaryman
tldr: The korean melon soju trend is about mixing soju with a popular melon ice cream bar, creating a sweet, easy-to-drink cocktail.
It's popular as of October 2026 due to its nostalgic taste, visual appeal for social media, and ease of preparation.
Foreigners can easily try it by buying ingredients at any Korean convenience store or ordering it at specific bars.
target_audience: This is for readers who are foreigners curious about current popular drinking trends in Korea and want an authentic, local perspective.
content:
📅 Updated 2026.10.04
Key takeaways
  • The korean melon soju trend is about mixing soju with a popular melon ice cream bar, creating a sweet, easy-to-drink cocktail.
  • It's popular as of October 2026 due to its nostalgic taste, visual appeal for social media, and ease of preparation.
  • Foreigners can easily try it by buying ingredients at any Korean convenience store or ordering it at specific bars.
👤 This is for readers who are foreigners curious about current popular drinking trends in Korea and want an authentic, local perspective.

Lately in Korea, you can’t scroll through social media or walk into a convenience store without bumping into the latest iteration of the flavored soju craze. As of October 03, 2026, the korean melon soju trend is everywhere, from university student gatherings to office hoesik (the after-work company dinner) I can’t escape. It's simple, it's sweet, and it's surprisingly addictive. If you’ve been wondering what's making Koreans grab a green ice cream bar with their soju, you're in the right place. Let me break it down for you.

What Exactly is the Korean Melon Soju Trend? (And is it Actually Good?)

The korean melon soju trend is, at its core, a DIY cocktail combining plain soju (Korea’s ubiquitous distilled spirit, usually around 16-20% ABV) with a specific brand of melon-flavored ice cream bar, most commonly the 'Melona' bar. You crush the ice cream bar directly into a cup of soju, stir until it's mostly dissolved, and boom – you've got a creamy, sweet, melon-flavored drink. It’s not a new concept in Korea to mix soju with sweet things, but this particular combination has exploded in popularity over the last year, especially among younger generations and those looking for a lighter, more palatable soju experience.

Is it actually good? Honestly, it depends on your palate. For me, after a long day at the office, a regular soju shot is sometimes too harsh. The melon soju makes it much smoother and sweeter, almost like a creamy melon milkshake with a kick. It masks the distinct alcohol taste that many foreigners, and even some Koreans, find challenging in traditional soju. My coworker, Manager Kim, swears by it on Fridays, claiming it helps him relax without the immediate 'punch' of straight soju. He even bought a pack of the melon ice cream bars to keep in the office freezer, which tells you how serious this trend is. For those who enjoy sweet drinks and want to try soju without the strong alcoholic bite, this is definitely a winner. For purists who prefer their soju neat, they might find it a bit too sugary and 'girly,' as some older guys at my hoesik would grumble.

Point: It's a surprisingly effective, sweet way to make soju more approachable, perfect for those who find traditional soju too strong.

How to Make Your Own Melon Soju: A Practical Guide for Foreigners

Making your own melon soju is incredibly easy, which is a huge part of its appeal. You don't need fancy bar tools or obscure ingredients. The beauty of the korean melon soju trend lies in its simplicity. You can whip this up at a convenience store table, in your guesthouse, or at a party with friends. I’ve seen countless people, myself included, doing exactly this. Here’s how you do it, step-by-step, just like I do when I'm too tired to think about anything complicated after work.

First, you need the right ingredients. A bottle of classic green-bottle soju (like Chamisul Fresh or Jinro Isul Toktok) will cost you about 2,000-2,500 won (roughly $1.50-$2 USD) at a convenience store or supermarket. Then, grab a 'Melona' ice cream bar, which is usually 1,000-1,500 won (about $0.75-$1.20 USD). You’ll also need a cup and something to stir with. Most convenience stores will provide a plastic cup and chopsticks if you ask.

When I first tried to make it, I made the mistake of trying to melt the ice cream first. Don't do that. Just crush it directly. It works better that way and gives it a nice texture. This isn't gourmet mixology; it's a quick, fun drink. The total cost for a single serving is usually under 4,000 won (about $3 USD), making it a super budget-friendly option for a night out or in.

Point: It's incredibly simple and cheap to make, relying on readily available convenience store items, making it perfect for spontaneous enjoyment.

Where to Find and Enjoy the Korean Melon Soju Trend in Seoul (October 2026)

As of October 2026, the korean melon soju trend is so pervasive that you can find the ingredients almost anywhere. The most common place, by far, is any convenience store (like GS25, CU, 7-Eleven, Emart24). These stores are on every block in Seoul, and they usually have a small seating area, perfect for a quick, casual drink. Just walk in, grab your soju and Melona, maybe a snack like tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes) or a ramen cup, and you're set. I often see university students gathered outside my local GS25 on Friday nights, doing exactly this.

Beyond convenience stores, many casual bars and pubs, especially those catering to a younger crowd in areas like Hongdae or Gangnam, have started offering melon soju on their menus. Sometimes they'll have a fancier version with actual melon slices or a special garnish, but often it's just the basic mixture. You might find it listed as 'Melon Soju Cocktail' or 'Ice Cream Soju.' Asking for 'Melona Soju' (멜로나 소주) will usually get the message across, even if it's not explicitly on the menu, as staff are very familiar with the trend. Some trendy cafes that also serve alcohol might offer a non-alcoholic version with just milk and melon ice cream, so be specific if you want the soju in it! I've even seen it pop up at a few of the more relaxed noraebang (karaoke rooms) lately, perfect for loosening up your vocal cords.

Point: The trend is widespread, easily accessible at convenience stores, and increasingly found on menus at casual bars across Seoul.

Why Did the Korean Melon Soju Trend Blow Up? (It's Not Just the Taste)

The explosion of the korean melon soju trend isn't just about the flavor; it's a mix of cultural factors that always seem to propel these specific soju trends. First, there's nostalgia. Melona ice cream bars have been a staple of Korean childhoods for decades. Combining it with soju creates a playful, adult twist on a beloved memory, making it instantly appealing. It's like turning your favorite childhood snack into a grown-up treat.

Second, visual appeal for social media is huge. The creamy, pale green drink looks distinct and inviting in photos and videos, especially on platforms like Instagram and TikTok. People love sharing their creations, and it’s an easy, photogenic drink to make. This viral sharing fuels the trend further, creating a constant buzz.

Third, and perhaps most importantly, it addresses a common barrier for soju consumption: the taste. Many people, especially those new to soju, find its strong, almost medicinal taste a bit challenging. The melon soju makes it incredibly easy to drink, almost too easy. This means people can drink more without feeling the burn, which can be a double-edged sword, but definitely contributes to its popularity. It democratizes soju, making it accessible to a wider audience.

However, there’s a downside. While tourists and younger crowds adore it, some older Koreans or soju connoisseurs find it a bit... overhyped. My boss, for instance, just rolls his eyes and asks for a regular bottle. He thinks it's a silly fad. And honestly, while I enjoy it sometimes, it can be a bit too sweet, especially after a couple of glasses. It's definitely a trend driven by youth culture and social media, rather than a deep culinary innovation. It's a fun, fleeting moment in Korea's drinking scene, much like the yogurt soju or fruit soju trends that came before it.

Point: The trend's success stems from nostalgia, social media virality, and its ability to make soju palatable for a broader audience, though it's not universally loved.

What's Next After the Melon Soju Trend? Keeping Up with Korea's Drink Fads

Korea's drinking scene is notoriously fast-paced, and while the korean melon soju trend is definitely hot right now in October 2026, it won't last forever. We've seen countless soju fads come and go, from the initial fruit-flavored sojus that swept the nation years ago to more niche concoctions involving energy drinks or yogurt. The key characteristic of these trends is often their simplicity, visual appeal, and ease of DIY. When I was in university, everyone was mixing soju with milkis (a milky soda). Now, that feels ancient.

Right now, alongside the melon soju, I'm starting to see a small buzz around 'yakgwa soju' (약과 소주), where the traditional honey-glazed pastry is crumbled into soju, creating a subtly sweet and slightly nutty flavor. It's not as mainstream as melon soju yet, but it's popping up on influencer feeds. The general pattern is that as soon as one combination becomes too common, people start experimenting with the next unusual pairing. It's all part of the palli-palli (the hurry-hurry, do-it-now mindset) culture – always on to the next big thing.

My advice for any foreigner wanting to stay current? Keep an eye on convenience store new product aisles and what young Koreans are posting on social media. That's usually where the next big thing starts. And don't be afraid to experiment! The worst that can happen is you make a bad drink; the best is you discover the next viral sensation. But for now, enjoy your melon soju while it lasts.

Point: Korea's soju trends are constantly evolving, driven by DIY culture and social media, with new, often sweet and visually appealing, combinations always on the horizon.

How it actually works

  1. 1
    Step 1: Gather Ingredients
    Head to any Korean convenience store (like GS25, CU, 7-Eleven) and purchase one bottle of regular soju (e.g., Chamisul Fresh) and one Melona ice cream bar. Grab a plastic cup and chopsticks if available.
  2. 2
    Step 2: Prepare Your Cup
    Open the soju bottle and pour about half of it into your plastic cup. You can adjust the ratio later based on your preference for sweetness or strength.
  3. 3
    Step 3: Add the Melon Ice Cream
    Carefully open the Melona ice cream bar. You can either break it into smaller pieces and drop them into the soju or, for a faster mix, crush it while still in its wrapper before adding it to the cup.
  4. 4
    Step 4: Stir Until Dissolved
    Use your chopsticks or any stirrer available to thoroughly mix the ice cream into the soju. Stir until the ice cream is mostly dissolved and the drink becomes creamy and pale green.
  5. 5
    Step 5: Enjoy Your Melon Soju
    Your homemade melon soju is now ready to drink. Adjust with more soju or ice cream if desired. Cheers!

Frequently asked questions

Q. What is the Korean melon soju trend?

A. The Korean melon soju trend involves mixing a bottle of plain soju with a melon-flavored ice cream bar, typically a 'Melona,' to create a sweet, creamy, and easy-to-drink alcoholic beverage.

Q. Why is melon soju popular in Korea right now (October 2026)?

A. It's popular due to its nostalgic connection to a beloved childhood ice cream, its photogenic quality for social media, and its ability to mask the strong alcoholic taste of soju, making it more approachable for many drinkers.

Q. Where can foreigners try the melon soju trend in Seoul?

A. Foreigners can easily try it by purchasing soju and a Melona bar at any Korean convenience store (GS25, CU) and mixing it themselves, or by ordering it at many casual bars and pubs that cater to younger crowds.

Q. What kind of soju is best for making melon soju?

A. Any standard green-bottle soju, such as Chamisul Fresh or Jinro Isul, works perfectly for making melon soju. These are widely available and cost-effective.

Q. Is the melon soju trend considered a long-term drinking custom or a passing fad?

A. Like many other flavored soju combinations, the melon soju trend is generally considered a passing fad, albeit a very popular one right now, driven largely by youth culture and social media rather than being a traditional custom.

한국 멜론 소주 트렌드: 서울 직장인의 솔직한 이야기

최근 한국에서는 소셜 미디어를 스크롤하거나 편의점에 들어설 때마다 최신 맛 소주 열풍을 접하게 됩니다. 2026년 10월 3일 현재, **한국 멜론 소주 트렌드**는 대학생 모임부터 직장 회식까지 어디에나 퍼져 있어 피할 수 없습니다. 간단하고 달콤하며 놀랍도록 중독성이 있습니다. 한국인들이 소주와 함께 녹색 아이스크림 바를 찾는 이유가 궁금했다면, 제대로 찾아오셨습니다. 제가 자세히 설명해 드릴게요.

## 한국 멜론 소주 트렌드는 정확히 무엇인가요? (그리고 정말 맛있나요?)

**한국 멜론 소주 트렌드**는 본질적으로 일반 소주(한국의 흔한 증류주로, 보통 알코올 도수 16-20%)와 특정 브랜드의 멜론 맛 아이스크림 바, 가장 흔하게는 '메로나' 바를 결합한 DIY 칵테일입니다. 아이스크림 바를 소주 컵에 직접 부수어 대부분 녹을 때까지 저으면, 짜잔 – 크리미하고 달콤한 멜론 맛 음료가 완성됩니다. 소주를 단 것과 섞는 것이 한국에서 새로운 개념은 아니지만, 이 특정 조합은 지난 1년 동안 특히 젊은 세대와 더 가볍고 마시기 좋은 소주 경험을 찾는 사람들 사이에서 폭발적인 인기를 얻었습니다.

정말 맛있나요? 솔직히, 입맛에 따라 다릅니다. 저의 경우, 긴 하루를 보낸 후에는 일반 소주 한 잔이 때때로 너무 강하게 느껴집니다. 멜론 소주는 훨씬 더 부드럽고 달콤하게 만들어주며, 마치 크리미한 멜론 밀크셰이크에 알코올이 들어간 것 같습니다. 많은 외국인들, 심지어 일부 한국인들도 전통 소주에서 어렵다고 느끼는 독특한 알코올 맛을 가려줍니다. 제 직장 동료인 김 부장님은 금요일마다 멜론 소주를 맹신하며, 스트레이트 소주의 즉각적인 '펀치' 없이 긴장을 푸는 데 도움이 된다고 주장합니다. 그는 심지어 멜론 아이스크림 바 한 팩을 사무실 냉동고에 넣어두었는데, 이 트렌드가 얼마나 심각한지 알 수 있습니다. 단 음료를 즐기고 강한 알코올 맛 없이 소주를 시도하고 싶은 사람들에게는 확실히 성공적인 조합입니다. 소주를 깔끔하게 마시는 것을 선호하는 순수주의자들은 제 회식 자리의 일부 나이 든 남자들이 불평하듯이, 너무 달고 '여자 같다'고 생각할 수도 있습니다.

> 요점: 소주를 더 접근하기 쉽게 만드는 놀랍도록 효과적이고 달콤한 방법으로, 전통 소주가 너무 강하다고 느끼는 사람들에게 완벽합니다.

## 나만의 멜론 소주 만드는 법: 외국인을 위한 실용 가이드

나만의 멜론 소주를 만드는 것은 믿을 수 없을 정도로 쉽습니다. 이것이 인기의 큰 부분입니다. 멋진 바 도구나 희귀한 재료가 필요하지 않습니다. **한국 멜론 소주 트렌드**의 아름다움은 그 단순함에 있습니다. 편의점 테이블에서, 게스트하우스에서, 또는 친구들과 파티에서 이것을 만들 수 있습니다. 저를 포함하여 수많은 사람들이 정확히 이렇게 하는 것을 보았습니다. 퇴근 후 복잡한 것을 생각하기에는 너무 피곤할 때 제가 하는 것처럼, 단계별로 만드는 방법을 알려드릴게요.

먼저, 올바른 재료가 필요합니다. 클래식한 녹색 병 소주(참이슬 후레쉬나 진로이즈백 같은) 한 병은 편의점이나 슈퍼마켓에서 약 2,000-2,500원(약 $1.50-$2 USD) 정도 합니다. 그런 다음, '메로나' 아이스크림 바를 집으세요. 보통 1,000-1,500원(약 $0.75-$1.20 USD) 정도 합니다. 컵과 저을 것도 필요합니다. 대부분의 편의점에서는 요청하면 플라스틱 컵과 젓가락을 제공할 것입니다.

처음 만들려고 했을 때, 아이스크림을 먼저 녹이려고 하는 실수를 저질렀습니다. 그렇게 하지 마세요. 그냥 직접 부수세요. 그렇게 하는 것이 더 잘 되고 좋은 질감을 줍니다. 이것은 고급 믹솔로지가 아닙니다. 빠르고 재미있는 음료입니다. 한 잔의 총 비용은 보통 4,000원(약 $3 USD) 미만이므로, 밤 외출이나 집에서 즐기기에 매우 저렴한 옵션입니다.

> 요점: 믿을 수 없을 정도로 간단하고 저렴하게 만들 수 있으며, 쉽게 구할 수 있는 편의점 품목을 사용하므로 즉흥적인 즐거움에 완벽합니다.

## 서울에서 한국 멜론 소주 트렌드를 찾고 즐기는 방법 (2026년 10월)

2026년 10월 현재, **한국 멜론 소주 트렌드**는 너무나 널리 퍼져 있어서 거의 모든 곳에서 재료를 찾을 수 있습니다. 가장 흔한 곳은 단연코 모든 편의점(GS25, CU, 7-Eleven, Emart24 등)입니다. 이 상점들은 서울의 모든 블록에 있으며, 보통 작게 앉을 수 있는 공간이 있어 빠르고 캐주얼한 음료를 즐기기에 완벽합니다. 그냥 들어가서 소주와 메로나를 집고, 떡볶이나 컵라면 같은 간식을 사면 준비 끝입니다. 저는 금요일 밤마다 동네 GS25 앞에서 대학생들이 정확히 이렇게 모여 있는 것을 자주 봅니다.

편의점 외에도, 특히 홍대나 강남과 같은 젊은 층을 대상으로 하는 많은 캐주얼 바와 펍에서 메뉴에 멜론 소주를 제공하기 시작했습니다. 때로는 실제 멜론 조각이나 특별한 장식을 곁들인 더 고급스러운 버전이 있을 수도 있지만, 종종 기본적인 혼합물입니다. '멜론 소주 칵테일' 또는 '아이스크림 소주'로 기재되어 있을 수도 있습니다. '메로나 소주'를 요청하면 메뉴에 명시되어 있지 않더라도 직원들이 트렌드에 매우 익숙하기 때문에 보통 의사소통이 가능합니다. 술을 파는 일부 트렌디한 카페에서는 우유와 멜론 아이스크림만으로 만든 무알코올 버전을 제공할 수도 있으므로, 소주를 원한다면 구체적으로 말하세요! 최근에는 몇몇 편안한 노래방(노래방)에서도 등장하는 것을 보았는데, 목소리를 푸는 데 완벽합니다.

> 요점: 이 트렌드는 널리 퍼져 있으며, 편의점에서 쉽게 접근할 수 있고, 서울 전역의 캐주얼 바 메뉴에서 점점 더 많이 찾아볼 수 있습니다.

## 한국 멜론 소주 트렌드가 폭발적으로 인기를 얻은 이유? (맛 때문만은 아닙니다)

**한국 멜론 소주 트렌드**의 폭발적인 인기는 단순히 맛 때문만이 아닙니다. 이러한 특정 소주 트렌드를 항상 추진하는 문화적 요인들이 복합적으로 작용합니다. 첫째, 향수가 있습니다. 메로나 아이스크림 바는 수십 년 동안 한국 어린이들의 필수품이었습니다. 이것을 소주와 결합하면 사랑받는 추억에 장난기 넘치는 성인용 변형을 더하여 즉각적인 매력을 선사합니다. 마치 좋아하는 어린 시절 간식을 어른용 간식으로 바꾸는 것과 같습니다.

둘째, 소셜 미디어의 시각적 매력이 매우 큽니다. 크리미하고 연한 녹색 음료는 사진과 비디오에서, 특히 인스타그램과 틱톡 같은 플랫폼에서 독특하고 매력적으로 보입니다. 사람들은 자신들의 창작물을 공유하는 것을 좋아하며, 이것은 쉽고 사진 찍기 좋은 음료입니다. 이러한 바이럴 공유는 트렌드를 더욱 부추겨 끊임없는 화제를 만듭니다.

셋째, 그리고 아마도 가장 중요한 것은, 소주 소비의 일반적인 장벽인 맛을 해결한다는 점입니다. 많은 사람들, 특히 소주를 처음 접하는 사람들은 소주의 강하고 거의 약 같은 맛을 다소 어렵다고 느낍니다. 멜론 소주는 마시기가 믿을 수 없을 정도로 쉽고, 너무 쉽습니다. 이것은 사람들이 알코올의 쓴맛을 느끼지 않고 더 많이 마실 수 있다는 것을 의미하며, 이는 양날의 검이 될 수 있지만 확실히 인기에 기여합니다. 소주를 대중화하여 더 넓은 청중이 접근할 수 있도록 합니다.

하지만 단점도 있습니다. 관광객과 젊은 층은 열광하지만, 일부 나이 든 한국인이나 소주 감정가들은 이것을 다소... 과대평가되었다고 생각합니다. 예를 들어, 제 상사는 그냥 눈을 굴리며 일반 소주 한 병을 요청합니다. 그는 이것을 어리석은 유행이라고 생각합니다. 그리고 솔직히, 저도 가끔 즐기지만, 몇 잔 마시고 나면 너무 달게 느껴질 수 있습니다. 이것은 깊은 요리 혁신이라기보다는 젊은 문화와 소셜 미디어에 의해 주도되는 트렌드입니다. 요거트 소주나 과일 소주 트렌드처럼 한국 음주 문화의 재미있고 덧없는 순간입니다.

> 요점: 이 트렌드의 성공은 향수, 소셜 미디어 바이럴, 그리고 소주를 더 넓은 청중에게 마시기 좋게 만드는 능력에서 비롯되지만, 보편적으로 사랑받는 것은 아닙니다.

## 멜론 소주 트렌드 이후에는 무엇이 올까요? 한국 음료 유행 따라잡기

한국의 음주 문화는 매우 빠르게 변화하며, 2026년 10월 현재 **한국 멜론 소주 트렌드**가 뜨겁지만 영원히 지속되지는 않을 것입니다. 우리는 수년 전 전국을 휩쓸었던 초기 과일 맛 소주부터 에너지 드링크나 요거트가 들어간 더 틈새적인 혼합물에 이르기까지 수많은 소주 유행이 오고 가는 것을 보았습니다. 이러한 트렌드의 핵심 특징은 종종 단순성, 시각적 매력, 그리고 DIY의 용이성입니다. 제가 대학생이었을 때는 모두가 소주를 밀키스(우유맛 탄산음료)와 섞었습니다. 이제 그것은 고대처럼 느껴집니다.

지금, 멜론 소주와 함께 저는 '약과 소주'에 대한 작은 화제를 보기 시작했습니다. 전통적인 꿀 바른 과자인 약과를 소주에 부수어 은은하게 달콤하고 약간 견과류 맛이 나는 음료를 만드는 것입니다. 아직 멜론 소주만큼 주류는 아니지만, 인플루언서 피드에 나타나고 있습니다. 일반적인 패턴은 한 가지 조합이 너무 흔해지자마자 사람들이 다음 특이한 조합을 실험하기 시작한다는 것입니다. 이것은 모두 빨리빨리(서둘러, 지금 당장 하는 사고방식) 문화의 일부입니다 – 항상 다음 큰 것을 향해 나아갑니다.

현재를 따라잡고 싶은 외국인에게 제 조언은? 편의점 신제품 코너와 젊은 한국인들이 소셜 미디어에 무엇을 올리는지 주시하세요. 보통 거기서 다음 큰 것이 시작됩니다. 그리고 실험하는 것을 두려워하지 마세요! 최악의 경우 맛없는 음료를 만들 수 있지만, 최상의 경우 다음 바이럴 센세이션을 발견할 수 있습니다. 하지만 지금은 멜론 소주를 즐기세요.

> 요점: 한국의 소주 트렌드는 DIY 문화와 소셜 미디어에 의해 끊임없이 진화하며, 새롭고 종종 달콤하고 시각적으로 매력적인 조합이 항상 지평선에 있습니다.

Lately in Korea, you can’t scroll through social media or walk into a convenience store without bumping into the latest iteration of the flavored soju craze. As of October 03, 2026, the korean melon soju trend is everywhere, from university student gatherings to office hoesik (the after-work company dinner) I can’t escape. It's simple, it's sweet, and it's surprisingly addictive. If you’ve been wondering what's making Koreans grab a green ice cream bar with their soju, you're in the right place. Let me break it down for you.

## What Exactly is the Korean Melon Soju Trend? (And is it Actually Good?)

The korean melon soju trend is, at its core, a DIY cocktail combining plain soju (Korea’s ubiquitous distilled spirit, usually around 16-20% ABV) with a specific brand of melon-flavored ice cream bar, most commonly the 'Melona' bar. You crush the ice cream bar directly into a cup of soju, stir until it's mostly dissolved, and boom – you've got a creamy, sweet, melon-flavored drink. It’s not a new concept in Korea to mix soju with sweet things, but this particular combination has exploded in popularity over the last year, especially among younger generations and those looking for a lighter, more palatable soju experience.

Is it actually good? Honestly, it depends on your palate. For me, after a long day at the office, a regular soju shot is sometimes too harsh. The melon soju makes it much smoother and sweeter, almost like a creamy melon milkshake with a kick. It masks the distinct alcohol taste that many foreigners, and even some Koreans, find challenging in traditional soju. My coworker, Manager Kim, swears by it on Fridays, claiming it helps him relax without the immediate 'punch' of straight soju. He even bought a pack of the melon ice cream bars to keep in the office freezer, which tells you how serious this trend is. For those who enjoy sweet drinks and want to try soju without the strong alcoholic bite, this is definitely a winner. For purists who prefer their soju neat, they might find it a bit too sugary and 'girly,' as some older guys at my hoesik would grumble.

> Point: It's a surprisingly effective, sweet way to make soju more approachable, perfect for those who find traditional soju too strong.

## How to Make Your Own Melon Soju: A Practical Guide for Foreigners

Making your own melon soju is incredibly easy, which is a huge part of its appeal. You don't need fancy bar tools or obscure ingredients. The beauty of the korean melon soju trend lies in its simplicity. You can whip this up at a convenience store table, in your guesthouse, or at a party with friends. I’ve seen countless people, myself included, doing exactly this. Here’s how you do it, step-by-step, just like I do when I'm too tired to think about anything complicated after work.

First, you need the right ingredients. A bottle of classic green-bottle soju (like Chamisul Fresh or Jinro Isul Toktok) will cost you about 2,000-2,500 won (roughly $1.50-$2 USD) at a convenience store or supermarket. Then, grab a 'Melona' ice cream bar, which is usually 1,000-1,500 won (about $0.75-$1.20 USD). You’ll also need a cup and something to stir with. Most convenience stores will provide a plastic cup and chopsticks if you ask.

When I first tried to make it, I made the mistake of trying to melt the ice cream first. Don't do that. Just crush it directly. It works better that way and gives it a nice texture. This isn't gourmet mixology; it's a quick, fun drink. The total cost for a single serving is usually under 4,000 won (about $3 USD), making it a super budget-friendly option for a night out or in.

> Point: It's incredibly simple and cheap to make, relying on readily available convenience store items, making it perfect for spontaneous enjoyment.

## Where to Find and Enjoy the Korean Melon Soju Trend in Seoul (October 2026)

As of October 2026, the korean melon soju trend is so pervasive that you can find the ingredients almost anywhere. The most common place, by far, is any convenience store (like GS25, CU, 7-Eleven, Emart24). These stores are on every block in Seoul, and they usually have a small seating area, perfect for a quick, casual drink. Just walk in, grab your soju and Melona, maybe a snack like tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes) or a ramen cup, and you're set. I often see university students gathered outside my local GS25 on Friday nights, doing exactly this.

Beyond convenience stores, many casual bars and pubs, especially those catering to a younger crowd in areas like Hongdae or Gangnam, have started offering melon soju on their menus. Sometimes they'll have a fancier version with actual melon slices or a special garnish, but often it's just the basic mixture. You might find it listed as 'Melon Soju Cocktail' or 'Ice Cream Soju.' Asking for 'Melona Soju' (멜로나 소주) will usually get the message across, even if it's not explicitly on the menu, as staff are very familiar with the trend. Some trendy cafes that also serve alcohol might offer a non-alcoholic version with just milk and melon ice cream, so be specific if you want the soju in it! I've even seen it pop up at a few of the more relaxed noraebang (karaoke rooms) lately, perfect for loosening up your vocal cords.

> Point: The trend is widespread, easily accessible at convenience stores, and increasingly found on menus at casual bars across Seoul.

## Why Did the Korean Melon Soju Trend Blow Up? (It's Not Just the Taste)

The explosion of the korean melon soju trend isn't just about the flavor; it's a mix of cultural factors that always seem to propel these specific soju trends. First, there's nostalgia. Melona ice cream bars have been a staple of Korean childhoods for decades. Combining it with soju creates a playful, adult twist on a beloved memory, making it instantly appealing. It's like turning your favorite childhood snack into a grown-up treat.

Second, visual appeal for social media is huge. The creamy, pale green drink looks distinct and inviting in photos and videos, especially on platforms like Instagram and TikTok. People love sharing their creations, and it’s an easy, photogenic drink to make. This viral sharing fuels the trend further, creating a constant buzz.

Third, and perhaps most importantly, it addresses a common barrier for soju consumption: the taste. Many people, especially those new to soju, find its strong, almost medicinal taste a bit challenging. The melon soju makes it incredibly easy to drink, almost too easy. This means people can drink more without feeling the burn, which can be a double-edged sword, but definitely contributes to its popularity. It democratizes soju, making it accessible to a wider audience.

However, there’s a downside. While tourists and younger crowds adore it, some older Koreans or soju connoisseurs find it a bit... overhyped. My boss, for instance, just rolls his eyes and asks for a regular bottle. He thinks it's a silly fad. And honestly, while I enjoy it sometimes, it can be a bit too sweet, especially after a couple of glasses. It's definitely a trend driven by youth culture and social media, rather than a deep culinary innovation. It's a fun, fleeting moment in Korea's drinking scene, much like the yogurt soju or fruit soju trends that came before it.

> Point: The trend's success stems from nostalgia, social media virality, and its ability to make soju palatable for a broader audience, though it's not universally loved.

## What's Next After the Melon Soju Trend? Keeping Up with Korea's Drink Fads

Korea's drinking scene is notoriously fast-paced, and while the korean melon soju trend is definitely hot right now in October 2026, it won't last forever. We've seen countless soju fads come and go, from the initial fruit-flavored sojus that swept the nation years ago to more niche concoctions involving energy drinks or yogurt. The key characteristic of these trends is often their simplicity, visual appeal, and ease of DIY. When I was in university, everyone was mixing soju with milkis (a milky soda). Now, that feels ancient.

Right now, alongside the melon soju, I'm starting to see a small buzz around 'yakgwa soju' (약과 소주), where the traditional honey-glazed pastry is crumbled into soju, creating a subtly sweet and slightly nutty flavor. It's not as mainstream as melon soju yet, but it's popping up on influencer feeds. The general pattern is that as soon as one combination becomes too common, people start experimenting with the next unusual pairing. It's all part of the palli-palli (the hurry-hurry, do-it-now mindset) culture – always on to the next big thing.

My advice for any foreigner wanting to stay current? Keep an eye on convenience store new product aisles and what young Koreans are posting on social media. That's usually where the next big thing starts. And don't be afraid to experiment! The worst that can happen is you make a bad drink; the best is you discover the next viral sensation. But for now, enjoy your melon soju while it lasts.

> Point: Korea's soju trends are constantly evolving, driven by DIY culture and social media, with new, often sweet and visually appealing, combinations always on the horizon.

mainEntity.name: What is the Korean melon soju trend?

step.name: Step 1: Gather Ingredients
step.text: Head to any Korean convenience store (like GS25, CU, 7-Eleven) and purchase one bottle of regular soju (e.g., Chamisul Fresh) and one Melona ice cream bar. Grab a plastic cup and chopsticks if available.

step.name: Step 2: Prepare Your Cup
step.text: Open the soju bottle and pour about half of it into your plastic cup. You can adjust the ratio later based on your preference for sweetness or strength.

step.name: Step 3: Add the Melon Ice Cream
step.text: Carefully open the Melona ice cream bar. You can either break it into smaller pieces and drop them into the soju or, for a faster mix, crush it while still in its wrapper before adding it to the cup.

step.name: Step 4: Stir Until Dissolved
step.text: Use your chopsticks or any stirrer available to thoroughly mix the ice cream into the soju. Stir until the ice cream is mostly dissolved and the drink becomes creamy and pale green.

step.name: Step 5: Enjoy Your Melon Soju
step.text: Your homemade melon soju is now ready to drink. Adjust with more soju or ice cream if desired. Cheers!
